purpose: Pre-GitHub-public sanitization: remove machine-specific host paths and usernames from tracked files; make the host-HOME isolation probes machine-independent without weakening the isolation boundary.
scope: path/username sanitization and probe portability only
out_of_scope_unchanged: Technocore protocol behavior, request semantics, cursor/poll_seq/resolved_seq/gap-detection logic
URL allowlist and read-only network boundary
Signer separation, private key / DID handling
Docker isolation policy, production supervisor design, VPS settings
security_property_preserved: The actual host HOME must not be visible inside the Observer container.

probe_mechanism.before: In-container isolation probes hard-coded the literal host HOME path (a personal '/home/<user>' string) and, in tests/live_smoke.py, a personal absolute path to the public repository canary file.
probe_mechanism.after: The host resolves its own real HOME path (pathlib.Path.home()) and the public repository canary path, and passes them to the container as the OBSERVER_HOST_HOME / OBSERVER_HOST_CANARY environment variables. The probes assert that the supplied absolute path is NOT visible inside the container. A missing, empty, relative, or root ('/') value makes the check evaluate False (fail closed / ISOLATION_FAILED), never an unconditional pass. No fixed username is substituted.
constraints_respected: host HOME contents are never read; no secret / seed / key / API-key access
host HOME is not mounted into the container
no Docker socket, key storage, or Windows filesystem mount added
OBSERVER_HOST_HOME / OBSERVER_HOST_CANARY are added to the container env allowlist (ALLOWED_ENV); the 'no unexpected env name' configuration check is unchanged in strength
no security assertion removed, skipped, downgraded to a warning, or made conditionally-passing

changed_files.tests/container_isolation.py: OBSERVER_HOST_HOME/OBSERVER_HOST_CANARY added to ALLOWED_ENV and to create_command (resolved on the host); embedded PROBE reads OBSERVER_HOST_HOME and asserts the absolute path is not visible, fail-closed. Canary check still uses the already machine-independent injected CANARY_PATH.
changed_files.tests/live_smoke.py: module-level CANARY now comes from OBSERVER_HOST_CANARY (empty when unset); process_checks() reads OBSERVER_HOST_HOME for host_home_absent and gates public_canary_unreadable on a valid absolute canary path, both fail-closed.
changed_files.tests/durability_payload.py: container_probe() no_host_home reads OBSERVER_HOST_HOME and asserts the absolute path is not visible, fail-closed. CORE_CHECKS key names unchanged.
changed_files.tests/run_durability.py: container_args() passes --env=OBSERVER_HOST_HOME resolved on the host.
changed_files.docs/durability-verification.md: four historical one-command examples changed from '/home/<user>/technocore-observer/tests/...' to '~/technocore-observer/tests/...'.
changed_files.docs/pre-vps-opus-audit.md: P3-2 finding and checklist item 10: personal path token neutralized to 'hard-coded host HOME path'. Finding, severity (P3 / NICE TO HAVE), file references, and historical judgement unchanged.

historical_artifacts.policy: Not modified. Per the repository convention (historical evidence is preserved; new state is recorded in a new artifact), the dated audit/regression artifacts intentionally retain the pre-sanitization source hashes of the tree they were run against.
now_stale_by_design: docs/pre-vps-p1-final.json / docs/pre-vps-p1-verification.json / docs/pre-vps-final-remediation.json (source_sha256 sections, where present)
historical_artifacts.note: These records describe historical executions on the pre-sanitization source. This sanitization is NOT presented as a re-run of those historical results.
